newsitem.title: USA: Figgie Q3 sales higher in 2 of 3 units.
newsitem.headline: Figgie Q3 sales higher in 2 of 3 units.

text.p: Figgie International Inc said Wednesday that third-quarter sales rose in two of its three core businesses and it expected sales in the other unit to rebound in the second half of 1997.

Sales of its Interstate Electronics unit, which makes guidance and naviation systems such as global-positioning satellite (GPS) systems, fell three percent from the 1995 third quarter, Figgie said in a statement.
For Interstate, "we expect to have a sales increase in the second half of 1997," chief executive officer Jack Reilly said in a conference call with analysts and reporters.
Figgie's third-quarter earnings per share rose to $0.36 from $0.06 in the same period a year ago.

The company also said it planned to sell its Taylor unit, which makes thermometers and weather-measuring devices, to a group led by Lawrence Zalusky & Associates, probably by the end of the year. It did not disclose the value of the proposed transaction.
Figgie's Scott unit, which makes fire safety equipment, recorded a 20 percent sales increase compared with the 1995 third quarter.
Its Snorkel unit, which makes telescopic booms and scissor-lift equipment for industry, showed a nine percent sales increase, the company said.
Reilly said he expected Snorkel sales to be even stronger now that customers were no longer concerned the company would sell the unit.

In July, Figgie said it was considering the sale of one or more of its remaining units, and Reilly said customers delayed some orders because of that uncertainty. On Wednesday, the company said it decided to retain Snorkel, Interstate and Scott.
